find.description: Find issues of the bound GitLab project by text, semantic state and labels, oldest first, one bounded page at a time. GitLab filters on state, labels and text in title and description; states map to labels through settings.states, and a closed issue is canceled by a canceled label or a duplicate link.

get.description: Read one issue of the bound GitLab project by its iid.

create.description: Open an issue in the bound GitLab project. The idempotency key is recorded in the description as a hidden comment: a repeated key returns the issue it opened, the same key with other content is a conflict, and a create whose outcome is unknown is read back and answered unresolved rather than opened twice. Only an issue the credential's account opened answers for a key; two concurrent calls with one key are not detected.

update.description: Change an issue's title, description or labels. Labels replace the task's labels; state labels change only through transition. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write: GitLab has no conditional issue write, so a writer between the two is not detected.

transition.description: Move an issue to a semantic state: the state labels settings.states names are swapped, and the issue is closed for done and canceled and reopened otherwise. A state other than open and done without a configured label is unsupported. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write.

assign.description: Replace an issue's assignees, named by username; @me names the credential's account. GitLab keeps only the users it can assign, one on a tier without multiple assignees, and the answer lists the actual assignees. An assignee is information, never an exclusive claim: this provider offers no claim.

find.description: Find the merge requests of an exact base and head in the bound GitLab project, by iid; head is a branch of the project, and a fork's branch is not served. A headCommit the branch already points at is awaited on an open merge request.

upsert.description: Update the open merge request of an exact base and head, or open it. GitLab keeps one open merge request per source and target branch, so a repeated or concurrent upsert never opens a second. A draft is the title prefix Draft:, which a proposal's title never shows; a requested title with a draft prefix is invalid. A requested headCommit must be the commit the branch points at. expectedRevision is compared with the merge request read just before the write. settings.assignAuthor adds the account's assignment; settings.inheritLabelPrefixes copies matching labels from the issues the description names in GitLab references (#12, project#12, group/project#12, issue URLs on the bound host). The answer lists the merge request's assignees and labels.

status.description: Read a merge request, the commit statuses of its head commit (pipeline jobs and external statuses), its review notes and its current approvals.

review.description: Publish a review as a note on a merge request that records its verdict, commit and idempotency key in hidden comments: a repeated key returns the note it posted, and a note whose outcome is unknown is read back and answered unresolved rather than posted twice. approve first approves the merge request at the reviewed head; request_changes first withdraws the account's approval, and GitLab blocks nothing on its note.

comments.description: List the notes people wrote on a merge request by note id, never a system note: a review note's body without its hidden comments, naming itself as its review, each diff note with its path, its line in the new file and the head commit it was written on, and each discussion note.

merge.description: Merge a merge request whose head is still the expected commit, sent as GitLab's sha. Refused before anything is sent unless settings.allowMerge is true; binding this provider authorizes nobody to merge. squash asks GitLab to squash; merge and rebase are served only where the project's merge method creates a merge commit or fast-forwards. settings.removeSourceBranch deletes the source branch in the merge call itself.
